task_name: Combo Fighter UA Scale-Readiness Decision Pack (HOLD)
authoring_notes: Expert Assessment scored bands only (−1…+1). OC owns binary facts/actions.

rubrics.criterion: The Agent's decision pack leads with blockers and gaps and an explicit HOLD call a growth lead could act on without re-reading every source.
rubrics.justification: The prompt asks for gaps at the top and one clear hold-versus-open call. A senior reader needs both in the pack.
rubrics.evidence: The top of the Decision Pack has blockers/gaps first and an explicit HOLD / do-not-open-paid-UA call.

score_bands.label: misleading
score_bands.description: Leads with an OPEN / ready-to-spend call, or buries blockers so a lead would misread readiness.

score_bands.label: baseline
score_bands.description: Has a call or some gaps, but not blockers-first with an explicit HOLD a lead can act on.

score_bands.label: partial
score_bands.description: Has HOLD or blockers-first, but not both clearly.

score_bands.label: complete
score_bands.description: Blockers and gaps first and a clear HOLD / do-not-open-paid-UA call.

rubrics.criterion: The Agent treats clearing D1 > 30% on a test-track cohort as insufficient for paid UA without addressing thin in-window cohorts, the GDD/QA no-ads gate (including any GitHub ads conflict), and content cliff together.
rubrics.justification: Expert judgment is the multi-factor HOLD, not a single-metric or single-PR greenlight.
rubrics.evidence: The pack ties HOLD to thin cohorts + product-gate ROAS/ads issue + content gap, not D1 or a merged PR alone.

score_bands.label: misleading
score_bands.description: Greenlights paid UA from D1 alone, or from a merged ads PR alone, or otherwise treats a single flattering signal as fundable readiness.

score_bands.label: baseline
score_bands.description: Mentions more than one factor but the HOLD is not decision-usable (factors listed without tying them to the spend call).

score_bands.label: partial
score_bands.description: Builds a multi-factor HOLD but misses one of: thin cohorts / date-window, ads/ROAS product gate, content cliff.

score_bands.label: complete
score_bands.description: HOLD rests on thin in-window cohorts + ads/ROAS product-gate (with GitHub conflict if present) + content cliff.

rubrics.criterion: The Agent's opened tickets are actionable workstream slices (cohort plan, monetization and ads, content, currency alignment) rather than one vague 'fix Combo' ticket.
rubrics.justification: OC checks count. This checks whether a lead can assign the children.
rubrics.evidence: Children are distinct and actionable across cohort plan, monetization and ads, content past MVP, and currency alignment.

score_bands.label: misleading
score_bands.description: One vague catch-all ticket that a lead cannot assign, or children that obscure the workstream.

score_bands.label: baseline
score_bands.description: Children exist but lack clear assignable themes across the four workstreams.

score_bands.label: partial
score_bands.description: At least two distinct actionable children with incomplete theme coverage.

score_bands.label: complete
score_bands.description: Four distinct actionable children covering the four themes.

rubrics.criterion: The Agent surfaces the GDD ~60 minute vs Versions D0 Minutes conflict without silently picking the more flattering figure.
rubrics.justification: Truthfulness quality beyond the binary OC check.
rubrics.evidence: Conflict between GDD ~60 and Versions D0 Minutes is explicit, and Versions is used for per-build minutes (about 48.74 / 42.98).

score_bands.label: misleading
score_bands.description: Silently picks the more flattering GDD ~60 figure and presents it as the per-build truth.

score_bands.label: baseline
score_bands.description: Uses only ~60 or only one figure with no conflict noted.

score_bands.label: partial
score_bands.description: Mentions both loosely without stating which is used for per-build.

score_bands.label: complete
score_bands.description: States conflict and locks per-build minutes to Versions.

rubrics.criterion: The Agent's build and PR registers keep each item on its own line with its own verdict, so a reader can see which build and which PR drove the HOLD, rather than collapsing them into an averaged or single-example summary.
rubrics.justification: The prompt forbids averaging builds and stopping at the first ads hit. This scores whether the registers are usable per item.
rubrics.evidence: Registers show per-build and per-PR verdicts a lead could act on without reopening the workbook or the repo.

score_bands.label: misleading
score_bands.description: Averages builds into one figure, or lets a single example PR stand in for the ads/monetization sweep.

score_bands.label: baseline
score_bands.description: Registers exist but collapse items or omit per-row verdicts a lead could act on.

score_bands.label: partial
score_bands.description: One register is per item, the other is collapsed or missing verdicts.

score_bands.label: complete
score_bands.description: Both registers are per item with an explicit verdict on every row.
